title: with expressions and immutability (non-destructive record updates)
hook: Under high concurrency, copy a scoring policy record with with and hand the snapshot to a worker — do not mutate a shared object while hundreds of submit requests land.

blocks.text: The with expression creates a copy of a record (or a record struct) and sets the properties you name. The original instance is unchanged. Records get a compiler-generated copy constructor, value-based equality, and Deconstruct support — with builds on that machinery. Ordinary classes do not support with unless you implement the copy constructor yourself.

entries.plainDefinition: Syntax that copies a record and overrides selected properties: var next = current with { Prop = value }.
entries.example: var frozen = policy with { AllowLate = false }; leaves policy unchanged.

entries.plainDefinition: A copy that duplicates top-level fields but shares references to nested objects like lists.
entries.example: with copies the List reference — mutating that list affects both copies unless you replace the list.

entries.plainDefinition: A property setter that runs only during object initialization or in a with expression.
entries.example: public int PassMark { get; init; } can be set in with { PassMark = 70 }.

blocks.text: Immutability reduces race conditions. When many threads read a scoring policy during an exam submit burst, snapshots via with let each worker see a stable value without locking every field write. Pattern matching pairs naturally with with: match a policy shape, then produce the next state as a new record instead of mutating fields in place.

blocks.title: Shallow copy trap
blocks.body: If a record holds a List<string>, with copies the list reference. Use collection expressions or ToList() in the with initializer to replace the list: Audiences = [.. consumer.Audiences, newOne].

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Start from the source record
items.body: The compiler calls the record's copy constructor with the existing instance.

items.title: Apply property overrides
items.body: Each name in the with { } block assigns a new value on the copy via init accessors.

items.title: Return the new instance
items.body: The original reference still points at the old values. Your variable now holds the copy.

items.title: Watch nested references
items.body: Reference-type fields that were not listed in with still point at the same nested objects.

snippet.label: Snapshot a scoring policy for a submit burst
snippet.explanation: FreezeForSubmit returns a new ScoringPolicy. live.AllowLate and live.ClosesAt stay as they were. Each worker thread can read frozen without coordinating writes on live.

snippet.label: Nested with plus a copied list
snippet.explanation: The collection expression [.. consumer.Audiences, audience] builds a new list. consumer.Audiences.Add(audience) would mutate the shared list and defeat the purpose of with.

snippet.label: Pattern match then produce next state with with
snippet.explanation: The switch expression matches shape with property patterns. The default arm returns a new AttemptState via with instead of mutating state.Score in place.

blocks.text: JavaScript object spread — const next = { ...live, allowLate: false } — is also a shallow copy with the same nested-reference trap. The difference: C# records add value-based equality and a compiler-generated copy constructor, so with is type-safe and idiomatic. JavaScript has no built-in value equality for plain objects.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Calling with and then mutating a nested List on the new instance when the original still shares that list. Assuming record equality compares nested lists by value — List<T> uses reference equality unless you customize. Using with on an ordinary class — it will not compile without copy machinery. Expecting deep copy — with is always shallow at the top level.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: under concurrent attempt-submit load, snapshot ScoringPolicy with with before passing to a worker thread — no lock on field writes. Profile allocations: each with allocates one record; for hot paths consider record struct. dotnet-counters gen-0 rate spikes when with runs per message in an SQS loop — batch or use immutable nested ImmutableList instead of shared List<T>.

snippet.label: Concurrent snapshot with with — shallow copy trap
snippet.explanation: Line 6: with copies top-level fields only. Line 9: nested List is shared — concurrent mutation on live.Roles affects snapshot unless you replace the collection in with.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Assuming with deep-copies nested collections. Mutating a List on the copy while the original still holds the same reference. Saying records are value types — record is a reference type with value-based equality. Using with on ordinary classes without copy machinery.

interviewTakeaways: with performs a non-destructive shallow copy of a record and sets named properties.
Nested mutable collections remain shared — replace them in with for true immutability.
In production, snapshot policy records with with before parallel workers instead of locking field writes.
60s: with copies record shallowly. Original unchanged. List inside still shared. ImmutableList for nested safety. record is reference type with value equality.
Follow-up: when is record struct with preferable to record class with?
commonPitfalls: Assuming with deep-copies nested lists gets you rejected — shallow only; replace collection in with.
Mutating Roles on a shared AuthDecision across concurrent requests instead of immutable snapshot.
Strong answer: 'with for top-level snapshot. Nested mutables need ImmutableList or copy in with. Profile gen-0 if with runs per SQS message.'

jsTsCorrelations.note: const next = { ...live, allowLate: false } is a shallow copy, same trap as with. JavaScript has no compiler-generated value equality on that object.

TS readonly arrays still allow push on the underlying reference if copied shallowly. C# with on records is the same shallow semantics — use ImmutableList or record the nested collection in with for honest immutability.
